To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The N-terminal SH2 domains of SHP-1 and SHP-2 have different pY-peptide recognition properties.

Molecular dynamics simulations on the SH2 domain of the SHP phosphatase reveal a mechanism for signal transduction where ligand binding induces domain dissociation by altering the conformational freedom and flexibility of the SH2-PTase binding interface.

Molecular dynamics simulations of the SHP2 SH2 domain in free and ligand-bound state show that pY peptide-binding induces conformational changes in regions of the SH2 domain that are involved in binding to the phosphatase domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular mechanism of signal transducer activation by SH2-peptide ligands.
the development of new methods for molecular simulations of biomolecules and their application to the study of the structural and dynamic properties of proteins.
the molecular mechanism that controls the allosteric regulation of SHP-1 and SHP-2, two important protein tyrosine phosphates that regulate cell growth and differentiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

pY-peptide ligands induce a conformational change in the N-terminal SHP-2 SH2 domain that reduces its capacity to bind the SHP-1 PTP domain, thereby facilitating SH2-PT domain dissociation and SHP-2 activation.

the SH2-peptide-binding site is not directly involved in the allosteric communication between the N- and C-terminal SH2 domains, but that the SH2 domain flexibility is modulated upon pY-peptides binding.
the pY-peptide binds to the N-SH-2 domain of SH2 and induces a conformational change, which in turn affects the binding of the SH2 domain to the PTP domain of SHP2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SH2 domain is a dynamic protein that can adopt different conformational states.
the SH2-PTPs have a unique mechanism of signal transducing that involves domain dissociation and that this is achieved by the SH2 domain allosterically modulating its own binding to the PTP domain.
the SH2 domain of the SHP2 tyrosine phosphates is an example of a protein domain which is allosterically regulated by ligand binding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the allosteric regulation of protein-protein interactions can be studied using molecular simulations.
the SH2 domain flexibility is an important factor in the SHP-1/2 signaling.
the allosteric effects of ligand binding are not necessarily restricted to the immediate vicinity of the binding site.
